Subject: Quick clarification on timeboxed POC pricing

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for yesterday’s demo — the team loved the low-latency generative routing examples. We’re lining up a 4-week, timeboxed POC for a chemistry-related internal tool. Before we finalize the SOW, procurement asked whether Redwood has a standard approach to: 1) one-time pilot discounts for evaluation-stage startups (we’re a small group within the company), and 2) whether unused hours/credits from a capped, timeboxed pilot can be converted to a pro-rated credit if we expand to a committed Dedicated pool later.

Two quick asks:
- Can you confirm the maximum discount AE’s can approve for a single pilot (or point me to the correct contact)?
- Any precedent for converting unused pilot capacity to a committed credit? If yes, what’s the usual conversion cadence?

We’re hoping to start the pilot week of Sept 2; procurement would like numbers to include on their internal approval thread. I attached the draft SOW the team put together.

Appreciate the help — Alicia

---

Subject: Re: Quick clarification on timeboxed POC pricing

Hi Alicia — great to hear the demo landed well. Attached is a short ratecard and a couple notes on how we typically handle the requests you flagged. High-level:

- One-time pilot discount: we can offer a single discretionary discount applied to the pilot invoice. Standard internal approval path: AE -> Sales Manager -> Rev Ops. Frontline AE (Ben) can approve up to 15% on pilot list pricing; anything above 15% needs manager approval.
- Unused capacity conversion: we have a pilot-to-commit conversion rule: unused timeboxed pilot credits may be applied as a one-time credit against a committed purchase if the customer converts within 60 days of pilot close. The conversion rate depends on whether the committed purchase includes Dedicated capacity (higher conversion) or Hosted units (lower).

For transparency, I’ve cc’d Ben (sales) and Priyom (solutions) to confirm we can hit the timeline and to propose an initial figure that procurement can use.

Naomi

If Priyom confirms there’s no unusual engineering burden (KV cache warm-up or custom kernel work), I’ll draft the email to procurement with numbers and a DocuSign link.

Ben

Hi Alicia / Procurement team,

Thanks for the SOW — attached is a concise purchase proposal you can include in your internal approval package. Summary of the proposal we can sign and execute before your Sept 2 start: 

1) Scope: 4-week timeboxed POC (Sept 2 - Sept 27), Hosted inference, up to 120k tokens/day peak.
2) Pricing: Pilot list price $8,500 USD (flat) for the 4-week timebox. Applied one-time pilot discount: 12% (final pilot invoice $7,480).
3) Conversion credit: If ChemBridge converts to a committed Dedicated purchase within 60 days of pilot close, any unused pilot value (unused portion of the flat pilot or unconsumed tokens) may be applied as a one-time credit equal to 70% of the unused pilot value toward the first Dedicated invoice. Credits not convertible to Hosted-only purchases.
4) Legal/Procurement: we can accept your typical PO flow; if Legal wants to redline the SOW, please send to legal@redwoodinference.com and we’ll turn around a response within 48 hours.

Next steps: I’ve attached the proposed purchase terms (two-page) and a DocuSign link. If this looks good, Alicia — please confirm and we’ll get the SOW signed so engineering can reserve the pilot capacity.
